key_insight: HVAF-sprayed Tribaloy-400 forms a denser, more protective oxide scale than detonation-sprayed T-400, giving better resistance to molten solar-salt corrosion at 500 °C.
engineering_relevance: For concentrated solar power thermal-storage containers, HVAF is the stronger coating choice when long-term exposure to nitrate salts and high-temperature oxidation are the main failure risks.
method: T-400 coatings were deposited on ASTM A516 steel by HVAF and detonation spraying.
Samples were exposed to 60% NaNO3–40% KNO3 molten solar salt at 500 °C for up to 1000 h.
Phase/SEM/EDS analysis tracked oxide formation, salt ingress, mass gain, and spallation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that HVAF retained a uniform Cr–Mo–Si–O enriched surface with minimal salt penetration, while DS showed deeper ingress, higher mass gain, and more spallation after prolonged exposure.
watch_item: Performance is demonstrated under one salt composition and temperature window, so coating selection should still be validated for real CSP cycling, thermal shock, and component-scale geometries.
paper_title: Hot corrosion behavior of thermal sprayed using HVAF and DS techniques with Tribaloy-400 coatings for solar energy storage container
